purpose: Velaglucerase alfa is used to treat a rare genetic condition called Gaucher disease. In Gaucher disease, a certain enzyme in your body is missing or not working properly, causing harmful substances to build up in your organs. This medicine helps replace that missing enzyme so your body can work more normally.
how_it_works: Your body normally makes an enzyme called glucocerebrosidase that breaks down a fatty substance. In Gaucher disease, this enzyme does not work well, so the fatty substance builds up in the liver, spleen, and bone marrow. Velaglucerase alfa is a man-made version of this enzyme that is given through an IV to do the job your body cannot do on its own.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include headache, dizziness, tiredness, nausea, stomach pain, joint or back pain, fever, and flushing or redness of the skin. Some people may have a reaction during or shortly after the infusion, such as chills, itching, or low blood pressure.
warnings: Tell your doctor right away if you have a serious allergic reaction during your infusion, such as difficulty breathing, chest tightness, severe rash, or swelling of your face or throat. Your healthcare team will monitor you closely during each infusion. Let your doctor know about all your medications and any allergies before starting treatment. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, talk to your doctor before using this medicine.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 60 units per kilogram of your body weight, given as an intravenous (IV) infusion every other week. Each infusion takes about 60 minutes and is typically given in a clinic or infusion center by a healthcare professional. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on how you respond to the treatment.
